topics.topic: Psychosis and acute behavioural disturbance
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: NICE and APA guidelines recommend verbal de-escalation as the first-line approach for acute behavioral disturbance. If pharmacological intervention is required, oral or intramuscular atypical antipsychotics (such as aripiprazole, olanzapine, or risperidone) or short-acting benzodiazepines are indicated while monitoring vital signs.
topics.references: Keepers, G. A., et al. (2020). The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia. American Journal of Psychiatry, 177(9), 868-872.

topics.topic: PTSD trauma-focused psychotherapy and SSRI
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: VA/DoD and APA guidelines strongly recommend trauma-focused psychotherapies (Prolonged Exposure, Cognitive Processing Therapy, EMDR) as first-line treatments for post-traumatic stress disorder over pharmacotherapy. SSRIs (sertraline, fluoxetine) serve as first-line drug therapy when psychotherapy is unavailable or declined.
topics.references: Department of Veterans Affairs / Department of Defense (VA/DoD). (2017). Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Acute Stress Disorder.

topics.topic: Pulmonary nodule evaluation and Fleischner follow-up
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: Fleischner Society guidelines outline specific criteria for managing incidentally detected pulmonary nodules on CT, using nodule size, morphology (solid vs. subsolid), and patient risk factors (smoking history) to dictate follow-up intervals or diagnostic evaluation.
topics.references: MacMahon, H., et al. (2017). Guidelines for Management of Incidental Pulmonary Nodules Detected on CT Images: From the Fleischner Society 2017. Radiology, 284(1), 228-243.

topics.topic: Pulmonary sarcoidosis corticosteroid therapy
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: ERS/ATS guidelines recommend systemic oral corticosteroids as first-line therapy for symptomatic pulmonary sarcoidosis or progressive parenchymal disease (e.g., declining FVC or diffusion capacity). Cytotoxic agents (methotrexate, azathioprine) or biologic agents (anti-TNF) are reserved for refractory or steroid-dependent cases.
topics.references: Baughman, R. P., et al. (2008 / updated ERS guidelines). Management of sarcoidosis. European Respiratory Journal, 32(3), 794-816.

topics.topic: Rabies pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: WHO and CDC guidelines recommend rabies pre-exposure prophylaxis for high-risk individuals. Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for potential exposures requires immediate, thorough wound washing, administration of human rabies immune globulin (HRIG), and a 4-dose series of rabies vaccine.
topics.references: Rupprecht, C. E., et al. (2016 / updated CDC guidelines). Use of a Reduced (4-Dose) Vaccine Schedule for Postexposure Prophylaxis to Prevent Human Rabies. MMWR Recommendations and Reports.

topics.topic: Radial versus femoral access for PCI
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline / RCT: ACC/AHA and ESC guidelines recommend radial artery access as the default approach for coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), supported by trials like MATRIX demonstrating significant reductions in access-site bleeding, vascular complications, and mortality compared to femoral access.
topics.references: Lawton, J. S., et al. (2022). 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization. Circulation, 145(3), e18-e114.

topics.topic: Radiation necrosis vs tumour progression: perfusion MRI and PET scan utility
topics.findings: • Clinical Consensus: Neuro-oncology consensus guidelines highlight that distinguishing radiation necrosis from recurrent high-grade glioma is diagnostically challenging on conventional MRI. Advanced neuroimaging modalities—such as dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion MRI, amino acid PET, or FDG-PET—are vital to guide surgical resection versus conservative observation.
topics.references: Ellingson, B. M., et al. (2017). Consensus recommendations for the use of advanced neuroimaging biomarkers in the assessment of neuro-oncology clinical trials. Neuro-Oncology, 19(9), 1189-1201.

topics.topic: Rectal cancer: total mesorectal excision, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: NCCN and ESMO guidelines establish total mesorectal excision (TME) combined with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (or short-course radiotherapy) as the gold standard treatment for locally advanced mid-to-low rectal cancers, significantly reducing local recurrence rates and improving survival.
topics.references: Glynne-Jones, R., et al. (2017). Rectal cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Annals of Oncology, 28(Suppl 4), iv22-iv40.

topics.topic: Rehabilitation after stroke: principles and evidence
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: AHA/ASA guidelines state that stroke rehabilitation should be coordinated by an interdisciplinary team. Intensive, goal-directed physical, occupational, and speech therapy should be initiated as soon as medical stability is achieved to optimize functional recovery and neuroplasticity.
topics.references: Winstein, C. J., et al. (2016 / updated 2021). Guidelines for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery: A Guideline for Healthcare Professionals From the AHA/ASA. Stroke, 47(6), e98-e169.

topics.topic: Retinal detachment: presentation and emergency management
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: AAO Preferred Practice Patterns dictate that rhegmatogenous retinal detachment is an ophthalmic emergency presenting with sudden flashing lights, new floaters, and a visual field "curtain." Immediate referral to a retinal surgeon for prompt surgical repair (scleral buckling, vitrectomy, or pneumatic retinopexy) is required to preserve vision.
topics.references: Flaxel, C. J., et al. (2020). Posterior Vitreous Detachment, Retinal Breaks, and Lattice Degeneration Preferred Practice Pattern®. Ophthalmology, 127(1), P146-P181.

topics.topic: Rh Alloimmunisation Management
topics.findings: • Clinical Consensus: ACOG guidelines recommend screening all pregnant women for blood group, Rh status, and red blood cell antibodies at the first prenatal visit. For Rh-D negative unsensitized women, routine administration of anti-D immune globulin at 28 weeks gestation and postpartum (plus indications for fetomaternal hemorrhage) prevents maternal alloimmunisation.
topics.references: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG). (2017). ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 192: Management of Alloimmunization During Pregnancy. Obstetrics & Gynecology, 130(5), e82-e94.

topics.topic: rivaroxaban treatment acute deep vein thrombosis EINSTEIN
topics.findings: • Landmark Trial: The EINSTEIN DVT trial demonstrated that single-drug oral rivaroxaban (without initial parenteral heparin) is non-inferior to standard enoxaparin/warfarin therapy in preventing recurrent venous thromboembolism while featuring a similar safety profile, transforming modern VTE management protocols.
topics.references: EINSTEIN Investigators. (2010). Oral Rivaroxaban for Symptomatic Venous Thromboembolism. New England Journal of Medicine, 363(26), 2499-2510.

topics.topic: rosuvastatin primary prevention elevated C-reactive protein
topics.findings: • Landmark Trial: The JUPITER trial proved that rosuvastatin significantly reduces major cardiovascular events in apparently healthy individuals with normal LDL-C levels but elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP ≥2.0 mg/L), establishing the clinical benefit of statins in primary prevention based on inflammatory risk markers.
topics.references: Ridker, P. M., et al. (2008). Rosuvastatin to Prevent Vascular Events in Men and Women with Elevated C-Reactive Protein. New England Journal of Medicine, 359(21), 2195-2207.

topics.topic: sacubitril valsartan heart failure reduced ejection fraction mortality
topics.findings: • Landmark Trial: The PARADIGM-HF trial established that the angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) sacubitril/valsartan is significantly superior to enalapril in reducing the rates of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization in HFrEF, shaping modern guideline recommendations.
topics.references: McMurray, J. J., et al. (2014). Angiotensin-Neprilysin Inhibition versus Enalapril in Heart Failure. New England Journal of Medicine, 371(11), 993-1004.

topics.topic: Sarcoidosis systemic immunosuppression
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: ERS/WASOG consensus guidelines indicate systemic immunosuppressive therapy (corticosteroids as first-line, followed by methotrexate, azathioprine, or infliximab as steroid-sparing agents) for organ-threatening sarcoidosis involving the heart, nervous system, eyes, or severe pulmonary fibrosis.
topics.references: Judson, M. A., et al. (2014). ERS/WASOG statement on sarcoidosis. European Respiratory Journal, 43(5), 1269-1281.

topics.topic: Scabies: diagnosis, treatment and outbreak management
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: CDC and dermatological guidelines recommend topical 5% permethrin cream applied from the neck down as the first-line treatment for scabies, or oral ivermectin as an effective alternative. Institutional outbreaks require simultaneous treatment of all contacts and thorough environmental laundering.
topics.references: Workowski, K. A., et al. (2021). Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021. MMWR Recommendations and Reports, 70(4), 1-187.

topics.topic: Secondary immunodeficiency from biologics and steroids
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: AAAAI consensus guidelines note that long-term systemic corticosteroids and B-cell depleting biologics (e.g., rituximab) frequently cause secondary hypogammaglobulinemia and impaired cell-mediated immunity, requiring vigilant infection monitoring, prophylactic antimicrobials, and consideration of immunoglobulin replacement therapy.
topics.references: Perez, E. E., et al. (2017). Update on the use of immunoglobulin in human disease: A review of evidence. Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, 139(3), S1-S46.

topics.topic: Sedation outside theatres and procedural sedation safety
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: ASA guidelines for procedural sedation outside the operating room mandate strict pre-procedural airway assessments, continuous monitoring of pulse oximetry, capnography, and blood pressure, and the mandatory presence of a qualified clinician dedicated solely to monitoring the patient.
topics.references: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Task Force on Sedation and Analgesia by Non-Anesthesiologists. (2018). Practice Guidelines for Moderate Procedural Sedation and Analgesia 2018. Anesthesiology, 128(3), 437-479.

topics.topic: Self-harm, suicide risk assessment and safe management
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: NICE and APA guidelines recommend comprehensive suicide risk assessments following acts of self-harm, evaluating intent, ideation, and protective factors. Safe management entails collaborative safety planning, restriction of lethal means, and prompt linkage to evidence-based outpatient mental health treatment.
topics.references: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE). (2004, updated 2022). Self-harm: assessment, management and longer-term provision. NICE Guideline [NG225].

topics.topic: semaglutide once weekly obesity weight loss STEP 1
topics.findings: • Landmark Trial: The STEP 1 trial demonstrated that once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (2.4 mg) combined with lifestyle intervention achieved a substantial, sustained mean weight loss of ~14.9% at 68 weeks in adults with obesity, reshaping clinical guidelines for obesity management.
topics.references: Wilding, J. P., et al. (2021). Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity. New England Journal of Medicine, 384(11), 989-1002.

topics.topic: sepsis bundle
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines emphasize protocolized "hour-1 bundle" implementation: measuring lactate levels, obtaining blood cultures prior to antibiotics, administering broad-spectrum antimicrobials within 1 hour, initiating rapid crystalloid fluid resuscitation (30 mL/kg) for hypotension, and applying vasopressors for persistent shock.
topics.references: Evans, L., et al. (2021). Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021. Critical Care Medicine, 49(11), e1063-e1143.

topics.topic: sepsis corticosteroids
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines suggest that low-dose intravenous corticosteroids (such as IV hydrocortisone at 200 mg/day) should be administered only for patients with septic shock whose blood pressure is poorly responsive to fluid resuscitation and moderate-to-high dose vasopressors.
topics.references: Evans, L., et al. (2021). Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021. Critical Care Medicine, 49(11), e1063-e1143.

topics.topic: sepsis diagnosis qSOFA SOFA criteria Sepsis-3 definition
topics.findings: • International Consensus: The Sepsis-3 consensus definitions define sepsis as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, identified clinically by an acute increase of ≥2 points in the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, while qSOFA serves as a bedside screening tool.
topics.references: Singer, M., et al. (2016). The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA, 315(8), 801-810.

topics.topic: sepsis early goal directed therapy
topics.findings: • Landmark Trial: Landmark multicenter trials (ProCESS, ARISE, ProMISE) demonstrated that protocolized, invasive early goal-directed therapy (EGDT) targeting specific central venous pressure and oxygen saturation goals does not improve survival compared to standard resuscitation protocols guided by clinical assessment.
topics.references: ProCESS Investigators. (2014). A Randomized Trial of Protocol-Based Care for Early Septic Shock. New England Journal of Medicine, 370(18), 1683-1693.

topics.topic: sepsis septic shock management surviving sepsis campaign 2021 guideline antibiotics fluids vasopressors
topics.findings: • Clinical Guideline: The 2021 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines provide updated recommendations, emphasizing early broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour, cautious and tailored fluid administration, and early norepinephrine infusion via peripheral or central access to maintain a mean arterial pressure target of 65 mm Hg.
topics.references: Evans, L., et al. (2021). Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021. Critical Care Medicine, 49(11), e1063-e1143.
